To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
beta amplitude in human motor cortex predicts the timing of behaviorally relevant cues, whereas the phase of slow oscillations in motor cortex entrain to the interval between these cues.
the beta amplitude increases from the start of a trial until the informative cue, and the delta phase entrains to the interval between cues-but only until that cue.
Beta oscillations in the hand area motor cortex predict upcoming behaviorally-relevant cues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional role of oscillatory activity in the motor system.
the functional role of beta oscillations in the context of movement preparation.
the role of beta oscillations in the motor system and their relation to movement planning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the beta oscillations are a marker of the subject's engagement in a motor task and the delta phase entrainment is a marker of the temporal structure of a task.
the oscillatory activity in the MI is a reflection of the subject's engagement in the task, and the beta oscillations in particular reflect the subject's anticipation of the task-relevant cues.
the oscillatory activity in MI is a reflection of a cognitive process, and the oscillation is not a cause of the cognitive processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
beta amplitude and delta entrainment in MI are related to the temporal structure of the task and predict the timing of behaviorally relevant events.
beta oscillations in MI are not simply a byproduct of the motor system but rather a mechanism for the subject to engage with task-relevant information.
beta oscillations in human MI are involved in the planning and preparation of movement and the delta phase in human MI is involved in the prediction of behaviorally relevant cues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the beta amplitude is not just a passive byproduct of movement planning but rather a dynamic signal reflecting the engagement with task-relevant stimuli.
beta oscillations in MI are not only a signature of movement execution, but also of movement preparation.
the rhythmic activity in the human MI can predict the subject's engagement and anticipation of behaviorally relevant cues.
